**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over 40 years. The winter wheat and summer maize rotation is what I know, what the market takes reliably, and what this flat, loamy ground in the North China Plain is suited for. I'm not switching to anything fancy at 62.

My concern this year, same as last year, is water. The well is pumping from deeper every season — everyone in the county knows this. I trimmed my irrigation schedule a few years back from four to three passes on the wheat and I didn't lose much yield. I'll hold to three again. For maize, summer rain usually carries it; I'll irrigate twice unless July is drier than expected.

I have about 12 mu of contracted land. Same 12 mu does wheat in winter and maize in summer — sequential, not split. My son helps with mechanical harvest. I hire the county seeder cooperative for planting.

For wheat I'll use Jimai 22 — it's what the county extension has been recommending and my neighbor got solid results last two seasons. For maize, Xianyu 335 hybrid is my standard. Proven kernel depth, good stalk strength for mechanical harvest.

I'll apply rotary tillage before wheat seeding in October to incorporate the maize stubble. For maize I direct-seed into the wheat stubble — saves time and fuel, and keeps the soil from drying out too fast after the June wheat harvest.

Fertilizer: I base-dressed too heavily when I was younger. I've cut back over the past five years based on what I've read in the county agricultural bulletins. I'll do a split application on wheat — base plus one top-dress at jointing. Maize gets a single side-dress at the 6-leaf stage.
